Name: Acidic Flask
Notes: 5 + [Clubs] stacks of Bleeding on hit. Suit-scaling added: a bare flip has exactly a 1-in-4 chance of matching a specific suit (1 card in the suit pool for an unmodified flip), so the marginal 6th-stack value (11.75-11.5=0.25) is credited at x0.25 -- 0.25 x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = 0.03125. Bleeding's Clubs pairing is the established convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, also matching Reckoning/Beast Venom's real [Clubs] Crippled text). Barely moves the needle since Bleeding is already near its ~12 asymptotic cap at 5 stacks. Value 1.28125, Net -1.71875, still an accepted below-budget utility item per the designer's earlier call.

Name: Immaculate Adhesive
Notes: 2 levels of Difficult Terrain in the target space and all adjacent spaces, lasting the encounter. Recomputed under the newly re-derived, non-linear Difficult Terrain curve (see design/balance_weights_notes.md) rather than the old flat 0.55/degree rate: 2 degrees hits the curve's hard cap at 8.25 (Agility-3/Speed-4 baseline). Guaranteed (no attack roll -- the effect auto-succeeds), so no hit-chance discount, but the flat Autoswing (5.5) opportunity-cost subtraction still applies same as every other Grenade. Priced for 1 creature actually crossing the full 2 degrees (the primary target, per the designer's own call -- only the one directly hit needs to cross the terrain at all), plus a half-credit margin (half of 1 degree's own value, 1.375) for the incidental area-denial value of a second creature losing an AP or so trying to cross it, or others taking suboptimal repositioning -- not a full second creature, since most of the party will just walk around the zone rather than commit to crossing it. Value 4.125, Net +1.125 -- deliberately a bit above the Level-1 threshold (0.8), since a genuine chokepoint should reward smart tactical placement rather than sitting exactly at budget. Net moves from the old flat-rate model's -6.3 to +1.125, resolving the structural ceiling problem flagged earlier in this pass.

Name: Bottled Fire
Notes: 8 Fire damage on hit (bumped from 7). Recomputed under the unified Grenade model: margin (8-3)x2=10, plus the +1 universal Harried credit any attack vs. Dodge/Parry grants, minus Autoswing (5.5) as the flat opportunity cost of not just attacking instead. Net moves to -0.5, within the Level-2 threshold (0.975) -- matches the same 1-damage-point bump the designer worked out by hand earlier in this pass, before applying it to the ledger.

Name: Smokejar
Notes: 3 + [Clubs] Crippled + a growing smoke/Heavy Cover zone for the scene. Suit-scaling added: marginal 4th-stack Crippled value (15-9=6) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.75. Clubs is the established Crippled convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, matching Reckoning/Beast Venom's real [Clubs] Crippled text). Value 6.25, Net +0.25, within the Level-2 threshold (0.975). (Difficult Terrain deliberately NOT suit-scaled here -- that was briefly considered for Immaculate Adhesive instead, a mix-up caught and corrected; Smokejar was always the Crippled-suit-scaling target.)

Name: Bonemelter
Notes: 3 + [Diamonds] stacks of Necrotic + 8 Shadow damage on hit. Suit-scaling added: Necrotic's marginal stack is linear (no stacking curve/cap the way Bleeding/Crippled/Vulnerable have), so the addition lands at full weight: 1.5 x 0.25(suit) = +0.375 (Necrotic's own situational-realization discount is already baked into its 1.5/stack rate, not reapplied). Diamonds is the established Necrotic convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table). Value 10.375, Net +1.375 -- a small overshoot past the Level-3 threshold (1.15), accepted as-is per the designer.

Name: Snowstorm
Notes: 8 Frost damage + Slowed 3 + [Spades] times on hit. Suit-scaling added: marginal 4th-stack Slowed value (11-6.6=4.4) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.55. Spades is the established Slowed convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, matching Spectral Spiderwebs/Beast Venom's real [Spades] Slowed text). Value 9.35, Net +0.35, still within the Level-3 threshold (1.15).

Name: Sunbeam
Notes: 9 Brilliant damage + Vulnerable 4 + [Diamonds] stacks on hit. Suit-scaling added: marginal 5th-stack Vulnerable value (14-10=4) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.5. Diamonds is the established Vulnerable convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table). Value 13.0, Net +1.0, within the Level-4 threshold (1.325).

Name: Hellfire Bomb
Notes: 8 Fire damage, hitting all creatures adjacent to the target (AoE, 2-enemy assumption). Recomputed with the AoE realization discount: (DamageComponent 20 + Harried 2) x0.8(realization) = 17.6, -5.5 Autoswing (undiscounted) = Value 12.1, Net +0.1 -- within the Level-4 threshold (1.325), resolving the overshoot flagged earlier this pass without touching raw Damage at all. See design/balance_weights_notes.md's AoE multiplier section for the full derivation (net 1.6x = 2x enemies-hit assumption x 0.8 realization).

Name: Thunderclap-in-a-Jar
Grants: Damage:16(post-AoE), Bleeding:2+[Clubs] per-target(AoE-multiplied, corrected), Harried:2+[Diamonds] per-target(AoE-multiplied)+2(universal, AoE-doubled)
Notes: 8 Physical damage + 2+[Clubs] Bleeding + 2+[Diamonds] Harried per-target, area-targeted (AoE, 2-enemy assumption). Recomputed under the corrected AoE-curve method (curve(N) x2, not curve(2N) -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md's AoE multiplier correction): per-target Bleeding(2)=8 + suit-scaled expected marginal (0.25 x (Bleeding(3)-Bleeding(2))=0.5) = 8.5, x0.5(on-hit)=4.25, x2(AoE, independent targets)=8.5. Per-target Harried-bonus(2)=2 + suit-scaled expected marginal (0.25x1=0.25)=2.25, x0.5=1.125, x2=2.25 -- unaffected by the correction since Harried is linear below its cap either way. Damage margin (8-4)x2=8 (per-target, linear, unaffected) x2(AoE)=16. + Harried universal (2, AoE-doubled) = total pre-realization 16+8.5+2.25+2=28.75, x0.8(realization)=23.0, -5.5 Autoswing = Value 17.5, Net +2.5. Lower than the previous (bugged) computation's +5.34 -- Bleeding's tapering curve was actually being under-credited by the old curve(2N) method, but the Damage margin (the larger component) is unaffected since it's linear, so the net change is still a real decrease. Still overshooting the Level-5 threshold (1.5) by a real amount, not just a rounding edge -- flagged for a follow-up decision (trim the Bleeding/Harried-bonus stacks, or accept as an intentionally-strong signature item), not resolved here.

Name: Reeler
Notes: Renamed from Quartz Tincture -- redesigned around a concussive, Harried-forward identity per the designer's call (a gap worth having in the Grenade lineup). 8 Fire damage (matching the L2-L3 sibling baseline) + 4 + [Diamonds] stacks of Harried on hit. Since Harried's own curve caps hard at 6 stacks (value 6 guaranteed / 3 discounted -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md), it can never carry much budget alone; going with Option B (genuine suit-scaling, base 4 usually landing 4-5, rarely 6) over flatly maxing it at 6 (which would make suit-scaling contribute nothing and read as misleading flavor text) or bumping raw damage to 9 (which would tie Sunbeam's Level 4 number). Value: margin (8-3)x2=10, Harried(4)=4x0.5=2, marginal 5th-stack suit credit (5-4)x0.5x0.25=0.125, +1 universal Harried, -5.5 Autoswing = 7.625. Net -1.375 -- an accepted below-full-budget item, same shape as Acidic Flask/Bottled Fire's earlier near-misses, prioritizing identity over hitting exact budget.

Name: Energizing Brew
Notes: Good Luck on Reflex (initiative), now until a full night's rest instead of 1 hour -- removes the guesswork of timing the drink to a specific fight without stacking extra value, since Reflex is still flipped exactly once per encounter no matter how long the buff is active (designer's explicit call, not re-priced upward for the wider window). Dropped AP:-2 entirely: same 'drunk ahead of time' reasoning as the prevention trio -- you'd have this active before initiative is even rolled, so it never actually competes with an in-combat action. Good Luck's own weight revised this session from 2.2 to 2.4 (see the Good Luck suit-pool correction in design/balance_weights_notes.md) -- GoodLuck(1)=2.4, Net = 2.4-3 = -0.6, clean fit at the Level-1 threshold (0.8).

Name: Fortifying Concoction
Notes: Grants 3 stacks of Protected (reduced from 4) -- never recomputed this session against Protected's own confirmed Locked value (3/stack, guaranteed), which left it badly overpowered at the old 4-stack grant: Value 12, Net +3.5 against a Level-1 budget, more than 4x over. Kept the standard full AP charge rather than the half-AP mixed-use treatment -- per the designer, Protected decays every round it's up, which makes it an inherently in-combat effect (unlike Healing Potion's genuinely split downtime/reactive use), so it doesn't get the same discount. Protected(3)=9, -5.5 AP = Value 3.5, Net +0.5 -- clean fit at the Level-1 threshold (0.8).

Name: Elemental-Attuned Tincture
Notes: Reworked around a redesigned universal Ward: +2 Resist while any stacks remain PLUS each stack can absorb 1 Health loss from that damage type (Protected's mandatory-substitution rule). Grants 3 stacks; these don't decay per-turn (alchemy convention, mirroring Poison), so the flat Resist piece prices at its full undiscounted rate (2.0 Fire, doubled per the Resist correction -- see balance_weights_notes.md). Absorption reuses Protected's own 3/stack rate scaled by the damage-share fraction (2/3): 2.0/stack, unaffected by the Resist fix. Fire: 2.0 + 3x2.0 = 8.0, Net = 8.0-6 = 2.0. Frost/Brilliant/Shadow: 1.0+6.0=7.0, Net=1.0 -- the absorption component still narrows Fire's usual edge.

Name: Essential Ointment
Notes: Draw 2 cards (bumped from 1) -- full AP structurally can't work for a card-draw item at this budget (the flat 5.5 AP tax alone eats most of a Level-2 target), so this moves to the zero-AP treatment instead: drawn cards sit in your hand until your next full night's rest regardless (per the Hand rules), so 'drink it before the scene' is the natural reading, same durability window the zero-AP convention already relies on for the prevention trio/Energizing Brew. Card:2 x 2.7 = 5.4, Net = 5.4-6 = -0.6, clean fit at the Level-2 threshold (0.975) without needing to touch Card's own value.

Name: Soldier's Salts
Notes: Regain the use of any Encounter Technique Level 2 or lower. THE TABEL has no 'refund an ability use' mechanic, so I used a trick: a refunded Technique use is worth that Technique's own Target budget (Level x 3). On its own that pins Value to exactly equal Target, giving zero margin to ever clear the item's own AP cost -- true of every refund-trick item, and why this whole family read badly at first. Fixed with a x1.5 premium on the refund's own baseline (same 'flexibility is worth something extra' reasoning Card's premium over Good Luck already uses), reused for Fighter's Friend/Battlemaster's Brew/Soul Soup below. Re-Leveled from 2 to 1 alongside the premium -- the item wasn't underpowered for what it does, it was costed one Level too high: at Level 1, refunding a Level-2 Technique, the fixed AP tax (a constant 5.5) finally stops eating more of the budget than the premium adds back. 1.5 x (2x3) - 5.5 = 3.5. Net moves from -5.5 to +0.5.

Name: Calming Brew
Notes: Prevents the next 4 total stacks of Taunted/Frightened this encounter (and removes existing stacks up to that total). Rebalanced to be drunk ahead of time -- AP charge dropped entirely (see balance.md): AP only matters in combat, and a 1-hour/pre-fight consumable spent outside initiative was never really competing with an attack. The reactive/emergency case (drinking it mid-fight) isn't separately modeled -- its cost is already implicit in the AP that use actually spends. Moved back to Level 3 (its original placement) rather than staying at Level 2, since 4x2.2=8.8 fits a Level-3 budget cleanly without changing the grant: Net -0.2, within threshold (1.15).

Name: Healing Potion
Notes: Heals 2 Health (Shallow, guaranteed) -- reverted back down from the earlier 3, replacing that bump with a half-AP charge instead. Per the designer: a lot of real use of the system's standard healing item is topping off Health outside of combat, where AP doesn't even exist as a resource -- but it's also genuinely used reactively mid-fight, unlike the L3 prevention trio which is overwhelmingly pre-fight prep. Charged at half the standard AP cost (2.75, 1 AP's value, instead of the full 5.5) to split the difference between those two use cases rather than assume either extreme. ShallowHeal(2)=8, -2.75 = Value 5.25, Net -0.75 -- clean fit at the Level-2 threshold (0.975). See balance.md for the new 'half AP for genuinely mixed-use items' convention this establishes, alongside the existing full-AP (always reactive) and zero-AP (always prep) treatments.

Name: Liquid Charisma
Notes: Good Luck on Presence/Persuasion/Rapport for 1 hour. Dropped AP:-2 entirely -- Social Contests don't spend AP as a resource at all (confirmed earlier this project), so charging AP for a purely social-flip buff was never actually correct. Replaced the old '~2 uses' guess with a real cadence estimate: a Social Contest resolves via a GM-set number of successes earned through Statement flips (Presence/Persuasion/Rapport), and the drinker, as the party's social lead, would typically carry most of the Statements in a scene running up to the full hour -- estimated at ~4 relevant flips, comparable in scope to a moderate combat encounter. Good Luck's own weight revised this session from 2.2 to 2.4 (suit-pool correction, see design/balance_weights_notes.md): GoodLuck(4) = 4 x 2.4 = 9.6, Net = 9.6-9 = 0.6, clean fit at the Level-3 threshold (1.15). Target = Level x 3 was calibrated against combat encounters, so this Net should still be read with that imperfect-fit caveat noted previously.

Name: Earthen Draught
Notes: Tops up to 2 Protected at the end of every turn for 1 hour. Since Protected doesn't stack past the current top-up, most of the ongoing value only matters if it's actually being spent down by incoming hits -- estimated as roughly 3 'refresh' instances worth of value over a 5-round fight (3 x 2 stacks = 6), not 5 refreshes, since some rounds won't need it topped up. Protected's own weight (3/stack) is unchanged this pass, just newly confirmed rather than asserted -- unchanged from the prior recompute.

Name: Fighter's Friend
Notes: Regain use of any Encounter Technique Level 3 or lower -- same refund-trick as Soldier's Salts, now with the x1.5 premium: 1.5 x (3x3) - 5.5 = 8. Re-Leveled from 4 to 3 as part of a reshuffled three-item family (Soldier's Salts now Level 1/refund-2, Fighter's Friend Level 3/refund-3, new Battlemaster's Brew below fills the vacated Level 4/refund-4 slot). Net moves from -5.5 to -1 -- a small, accepted gap, same tier as several other items this session.

Name: Swiftblade Vial
Notes: Redesigned to drop Good Luck entirely, per the designer's call to separate this from Fatebinder's Cordial's identity and lean into a purely speed/tempo theme instead. First explored a direct Extra Success grant, rejected on a new standing rule (design/RULES_DESIGN.md) -- damage/success bonuses stay routed through Good Luck/Defense-reduction/Gambling/suit-pool assists, never granted flat. Landed on turn-order adjustment instead, a mechanic the designer wants to use more broadly and which had no existing value in this model -- first derivation this session, Pencil 1.0/place (see balance_weights_notes.md). Hasted(8) = 0.55x(4x8-6) = 14.3, + TurnOrder(3) = 3.0, = 17.3, -5.5 AP = Value 11.8, Net = 11.8-12 = -0.2, clean fit at the Level-4 threshold (1.325). An earlier draft tried carrying more of the budget through turn-order alone (~9 places against a modest Hasted count) -- far past any existing precedent's scale, which is what pushed this final split toward a smaller, still-untested shift paired with a bigger Hasted component instead.

Name: Battlemaster's Brew
Notes: New item, filling the Level 4 slot vacated when Fighter's Friend re-Leveled down to 3. Regain the use of any Encounter Technique Level 4 or lower -- same refund-trick and x1.5 premium as its siblings: 1.5 x (4x3) - 5.5 = 12.5. Net lands at +0.5, completing the family: Soldier's Salts (L1, refund-2, +0.5), Fighter's Friend (L3, refund-3, -1), Battlemaster's Brew (L4, refund-4, +0.5).

Name: Insanity Potion
Notes: Full rework this pass, replacing the old 'treat any card as a Heart' clause (a leftover from a previous rules version meant to guarantee a damage bonus, no longer needed now that Extra Successes route through Good Luck/suit matching/Gambling) with a Battle Maneuver Battering-style effect: if your attack hits or is Parried, the target gains a stack of Bleeding, running for the whole hour rather than a single proc. Speed(1, non-decaying for the whole encounter) = 0.55 x 4 turns = 2.2 (corrected from the old flat 0.55, which only priced the first-turn marginal). Crippled/Slowed immunity priced as an average, not a sum, of Crippled(3)=9 and Slowed(2)=3.3 -- a fight realistically throws one debuff type at a target, not both at once (same logic Predator's Cry's own Crippled-or-Slowed clause uses) -- average = 6.15. Wounded immunity triangulated two ways (flip-based: ~2 turns x 1 attack+1 defense flip x Bad Luck's 2.2 = 8.8; opportunity-cost: saving the party Healer 2 AP = 5.5; averaged = 7.15) but then assumed, per the designer, to roughly offset the item's own drawback (cannot heal or gain Protected for the hour) rather than pricing both independently -- the drawback exists specifically as a countermeasure to this one piece, so netting them to 0 is more faithful to the original intent than deriving both separately and hoping they happen to cancel. Sustained Bleeding-on-hit priced at Bleeding's own hard cap (12), not a per-proc multiply, since stacks reapplied throughout a whole encounter against one focused target accumulate faster than the 1/turn decay unwinds them. Total = 2.2+6.15+12.0 = 20.35, -5.5 AP = Value 14.85, Net = 14.85-15 = -0.15 -- landing close to neutral by design: per the designer, a capstone item is meant to be a little swingy (stronger in some contexts, offset by its own real drawback in others), with the 'reward cleverness and risk over raw power' principle (see RULES_DESIGN.md) doing more of the work than an inflated Net would.

Name: Kiss of the Earth
Notes: Prevents the next 3 stacks of Bleeding, 1 hour (reduced from 4, and now also removes existing stacks up to that total -- matches Calming Brew's existing wording). Rebalanced to be drunk ahead of time -- AP charge dropped entirely (see balance.md), same reasoning as Calming Brew. Bleeding(3)=10 fits a Level-3 budget cleanly (moved up from Level 2): Net +1.0, within threshold (1.15).

Name: Predator's Cry
Notes: Prevents the next 3 stacks of Crippled or Slowed, until next rest (reduced from 4, moved Level 4->3 to consolidate all three stack-prevention Potions -- Calming Brew, Kiss of the Earth, this one -- into a single Level-3 'preparation item' cluster per the designer's healing-family framework). avg(Crippled(3)=9, Slowed(3)=6.6)=7.8, no AP (drunk ahead of time). Net -1.2, just outside the Level-3 threshold (1.15) by a negligible margin -- accepted as-is.

Name: Revivification Draught
Grants: DeepHeal:4(ticks, player choice of Shallow or Deep), AP:-2
Notes: Reworked from a Level 5 burst-heal (5 immediately + 1/turn for 4 rounds) into a Level 4 pure trickle: 1 Health, player's choice of Shallow or Deep, at the start of each of the next 4 turns. Frees up Level 5 for a different capstone item and gives the healing-Potion family a dedicated 'prevent Wounded over time' option per the designer's framework (L1 Fortifying Concoction/Protected, L2 Healing Potion, L3 stack-prevention cluster, L4 this). Priced at Deep Heal's own rate (5/point) since the Shallow-or-Deep choice belongs to the player, not chance or an enemy -- same 'price the rational best choice' logic as any other player-controlled option, not averaged the way Crippled-or-Slowed was (that choice belongs to the enemy). 4 x 5 = 20, -5.5 AP (kept standard -- explicitly meant to work mid-combat, not just downtime prep, so it doesn't get the 'drunk ahead of time' AP exemption the L3 prevention cluster gets) = Value 14.5, Net +2.5. A deliberate overshoot past the Level-4 threshold (1.325), accepted per the designer given healing's own pricing tension: reactive timing flexibility (apply after you already know the damage landed, no need to predict an incoming hit) versus the rigidity of a fixed per-turn trickle when a player actually needs a lot of healing right now.

Name: Basic Poison
Notes: Structural/carrier item only -- sets Concentration (3+Level) and Potency (=Level) for whichever of the 7 flavors below is chosen; has no standalone mechanical grant of its own, so no Value/Net computed for this row specifically. See I050-I056 for the actual priced flavors, each shown combined with a representative Level-3 Basic Poison (Potency 3).

Name: Crippling Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3 (Potency 3): 3 stacks Crippled on a successful poison-attack. AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both DROPPED this session -- see design/balance.md's Poison entry. Per the designer, every Poison effect except Bleeding persists ~1 hour per stack rather than decaying via the normal 1/turn Fleeting rule -- so Crippled's own compounding curve (which assumes decay across its 2-turn survival window) needs its stack count held at FULL strength across both turns instead of tapering: 1.5 x 3 x 2 = 9, not the decaying-curve's 7.5. Net lands at exactly 0 -- no adjustment needed, this item is naturally balanced once every correction is applied. Its 1x-Potency stack grant (vs. Bloody/Necrotic Poison's 2x) turns out to be the right baseline multiplier for a keyword at Crippled's rate.

Name: Bloody Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3: 6 stacks Bleeding (twice Potency) via weapon application -- the ingested version (4x Potency) isn't modeled here since that requires a completely different delivery method, out of scope for a weapon-poison assumption. Bleeding's own curve caps hard at high stack counts (6 stacks = 11.75). AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both DROPPED, same as the rest of the batch. Unlike every other Poison, Bleeding is the one explicitly called out as expiring NORMALLY (standard 1/turn Fleeting decay, not the ~1 hour/stack persistence the rest of this batch gets) -- so its curve doesn't get the same full-strength-across-2-turns adjustment Crippling/Slowing/Vulnerability/Harrying Poison do below. REVIEWED AND LEFT AS-IS: Net +2.75 is a deliberate exception, not a gap -- the designer likes a strong-enough Bleeding poison being able to threaten a kill outright, doesn't expect the full stack count to matter much in a real pitched fight (focus-fire kills things before Bleeding's tail value fully realizes, same caveat as every other Bleeding-granting item), and it isn't out of line with Acidic Flask's own similar +2.5 Net under the same curve. No item-text change.

Name: Slowing Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3 (1x Potency, unchanged): 3 stacks Slowed. AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both dropped, same as the rest of the batch; persists at full strength across the whole 4-turn window (capped at 4 stacks) rather than decaying, same treatment as the other Poison-delivered curves. Slowed's own base rate doubled this session (a Slowed target needs two movement actions per turn, both hit by the same flat penalty) from 0.55 to 1.1/stack: 1.1 x 3 x 4 x 0.5 = 6.6, not the pre-doubling curve's 3.3. Net moves from -5.7 to -2.4 -- checked across Levels 1-5, holds at a consistent -0.8 to -3.2 through Level 4 before the 4-stack cap starts widening the gap at Level 5 (-6.2). Close enough now that no multiplier change seems warranted -- same call as Vulnerability/Harrying Poison.

Name: Necrotic Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3: 9 stacks Necrotic (three times Potency, bumped from twice -- see below). Necrotic has its own derived value (3/stack when it resolves) rather than generic Debuff, and this poison's decay now follows the generic [Poison] rule (1 stack/hour) like every other flavor, after its own special '2 stacks/hour' carve-out was tidied away this session. Applies a 'does the situation actually come up' discount (x0.75, reflecting that ~1hr/stack persistence gives it plenty of time to actually catch a heal attempt or a Protected grant) and the standard poison-roll discount every Poison in this batch carries (x0.5, reinstated this session after being briefly dropped in error -- this row's own Value was left stale at 13.5/+4.5 through that whole pass and only now catches up): 9 x 3 x 0.75 x 0.5 = 10.125. Unlike Crippled/Vulnerable/Slowed, Necrotic has no stacking cap, so its fit is purely linear -- at the old 2x-Potency grant it read a clean, constant -25% under Target at every Level; bumped to 3x for a tighter (and now slightly over instead of under) constant +12.5% fit, accepted as fine for what's already a fairly niche pick.

Name: Vulnerability Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency (matching Bloody Poison's own precedent), fixing a real shortfall: Crippling Poison's 1x multiplier lands exactly on Target because Crippled's own per-stack rate (1.5) is high enough at that multiplier, but Vulnerable's rate (1) can't reach Target the same way at 1x -- not a poison-specific issue, just a lower-rate keyword needing a bigger multiplier to match. Representative Level 3 (Potency 3, so 6 stacks): full-strength-across-the-2-turn-window formula 1 x 6 x 2 = 12, Net = 12-9 = 3. An accepted overshoot, same magnitude as Bloody Poison's own +2.75 -- per the designer, Poisons can reasonably carry a wider balance berth than other items (single-target, and a dedicated alchemist gets more value from steady low-Level use than from maxing out Potency for one huge application), so the top end running a bit hot isn't the primary concern.

Name: Harrying Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency, same fix and same reasoning as Vulnerability Poison above -- Harrying Poison already reuses Vulnerable's exact formula (continuously-active penalty against incoming threats for the ~1hr/stack survival window, not Harried's normal one-shot-per-turn shape), so it needed the same multiplier bump for the same reason. Representative Level 3 (6 stacks): 1 x 6 x 2 = 12, Net = 12-9 = 3. Same accepted-overshoot call as Vulnerability Poison.

Name: Psychosis Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency, same fix as Vulnerability/Harrying Poison. Representative Level 3 (6 stacks): 6 x 2.2 (Frightened's own rate) x 0.75 (future-hit-lands discount, loosened from 0.5 to reflect the ~1hr persistence window) = 9.9, Net = 9.9-9 = 0.9 -- a genuinely clean fit, the best-landing of the three bumped this pass.

Name: Travel Rations
Notes: Pure logistics item (a day's food, never spoils) -- grants no combat-facing mechanic at all. Out of scope for this Value model; left at Value 0 / Net = -Target rather than force a meaningless number. Not a balance concern, just not what this model prices. [Target corrected to Level x6 (6) per the once/day formula fix -- Net now -6.0. Not re-tuned; flagged for review since this changes a pre-existing, previously-settled Food item, not new work from this pass.]

Name: Power Snack
Notes: Sift 6 cards (Level x6), using the corrected Sift weight (~0.60/card -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md; simulated value captured within ~18 draws/day, derived from Baseline's own attack-frequency numbers, not the old sheet's unexplained 0.64). Rate and Target both scoped to 'per day' consistently (Rate=1, Target=Level x 4 for a once-daily item, per the corrected once-per-day convention). No weight used here changed further this pass -- unchanged from the prior recompute. [Target corrected to Level x6 (6) per the once/day formula fix -- Net now -2.39. Not re-tuned; flagged for review since this changes a pre-existing, previously-settled Food item, not new work from this pass.]

Name: Hearty Meal
Notes: Heals an extra 1 Shallow Health (Level) on the next full night's rest, guaranteed. Rate=1/Target=Level x 4 (once-per-day convention). Lands exactly at Net 0, the cleanest result in the whole Food batch. No weight used here changed this pass -- unchanged. [Target corrected to Level x6 (6) per the once/day formula fix -- Net now -2.0. Not re-tuned; flagged for review since this changes a pre-existing, previously-settled Food item, not new work from this pass.]

Name: Muscular Feast
Grants: Bleeding:2(prevented) or Crippled:2(prevented) or Slowed:2(prevented), AP:0

Name: Legbreaker
Notes: 8 Physical damage + 3-meter Push on hit (trimmed from 4m). Rechecked after Push's own rate was decoupled from Speed and re-derived (0.89375/meter, up from 0.55/meter) -- at the old 4m distance this would have become Value=7.075, Net=+1.075 (118% funded), a real overshoot. Trimmed to 3m instead: margin (8-4)x2=8 (Physical Resist placeholder 4) + Push 3m x0.89375=2.68125 + universal Harried(1) - Autoswing(5.5) = Value 6.181, Net=+0.18 (103% funded), restoring the same close-to-Target shape the original 4m/old-rate version had.

Name: Harrowing Ichor
Notes: 7 Shadow damage + 2 + [Hearts] stacks of Frightened on hit. Second of two new Grenades drafted to add mechanical variety (fills the completely-untouched Frightened keyword -- no existing Grenade granted it). Priced under the unified Grenade model: margin (7-3)x2=8, Frightened(2)=4.4 halved to 2.2 for the on-hit contingency, plus suit-scaled marginal 3rd-stack credit (2.2x0.5x0.25=0.275), +1 universal Harried, -5.5 Autoswing = Value 5.975, Net -0.025. Deliberately 1 point below Bottled Fire's own damage (7 vs 8) so it trades raw margin for the Frightened rider rather than being strictly better.

Name: Oozejar
Notes: AoE, no Damage component. Per-target: Slowed(4)=11, Crippled(3)=9, summed then x0.5(on-hit)=10 -- this is the value delivered to ONE target. AoE doubles that (x2, two independent targets, NOT double the stacks fed into one curve evaluation -- see the AoE multiplier correction in design/balance_weights_notes.md) = 20, + Harried universal (2, AoE-doubled) = 22, x0.8(realization) = 17.6, -5.5 Autoswing = Value 12.1, Net +0.1 -- a very clean fit at Level 4. Asymmetric stack counts (4 Slowed/3 Crippled, not 4/4) were needed to land here -- 4/4 overshot badly (+4.9) even under the corrected model, since concentrating a lot of value in two still-climbing curves adds up fast. Real play value likely exceeds even this number -- an immobilized-and-barely-functional target is closer to fully removed from the fight than the flip-chance math alone captures (same acknowledged-conservative-floor reasoning as Slowed/Harried elsewhere).

Notes: Moved down from Level 2, Hasted trimmed 7->5, per the designer's call to keep L1/L2 buff potions simple and single-mechanic. Hasted(5) = 0.55 x (4x5-6) = 7.7, -5.5 AP = Value 2.2, Net = 2.2-3 = -0.8, right at the edge of the Level-1 threshold (0.8) -- a clean fit.

Name: Spellblade's Sipper
Notes: Renamed from Warmage's Draft. Rebalanced so the two components carry roughly equal weight. ElementalConvert(4) = 4x2 = 8 (unaffected by the Resist fix -- uses Damage's own rate). Name: Fatebinder's Cordial

The card draw is contingent on landing a Down, but per the standing 'does the threat show up' discount removal for consumables, a rational player only drinks this when a kill is imminent, so it prices at full value: 2xCard(2.7) = 5.4. Name: Elemental Warding Band (L1)
Notes: RENAMED from "Elemental Warding Amulet" -- was always Slot:Ring in the original source doc, just oddly named/flavored (not mis-tagged); no mechanical change from the rename alone. Once/encounter, grant 1 stack of chosen-type Ward (2 if Level 2) to self or a willing creature touched. [Supersedes this row's earlier pre-rework value, which predated the rename/reflavor and the +15% targeting-flexibility bump.]

Name: Armor of Constitutional Integrity
Notes: Cut its Neck-slot duplicate, Periapt of Constitutional Integrity (I175) -- word-for-word identical text, and a clear mismatch for Neck's own design lane ('niche, boring, passive utility, deliberately not defensive' per RULES_DESIGN.md's slot philosophy) -- almost certainly a pre-slot-philosophy leftover never reconciled once Torso became the defense-designated slot. Widened this item's own trigger from Poison-only to 'Poison, Disease, or similar bodily threat' to match Resilience's own stated domain ('resisting the adverse effects of poison, disease, exhaustion...'), raising how often it's actually relevant. Per the designer: Poison alone comes up roughly 1 in 2-3 fights (used 0.4), hitting ~2 instances per player when it does; widening the trigger category bumps that to an estimated 0.5. BadLuck: 0.5 x 2 x 2.2 = 2.2. GoodLuck(Resilience, permanent, ~1 flip/encounter assumed) = 2.4. Total = 4.6, Net = 4.6-6 = -1.4 -- a real improvement from the pure-Poison version's -1.84 (which was itself already better than the original -3.05 before the frequency was refined), and close enough to accept under the same Masterwork-berth allowance as the Torso Resist items.

Name: Lifeforce Plate (L3)
Notes: At the end of the wearer's turn, refill to 1 stack of Protected if at 0. Priced against the broader "~2.5 relevant empty moments/encounter" read of that trigger (not the stricter 1.875-hits anchor used elsewhere for a guaranteed major hit) -- Lifeforce Plate's trigger also catches incidental chip damage, not just the big swing, so the wider count is the better fit. Considered and rejected: pricing as "assume every one of the 1.875 hits/player/encounter lands while this item's Protected is up," which collapses back to treating the raw hit-count itself as the refill frequency with no discount -- mathematically reproduces the original, stricter estimate almost exactly (Net -3.375 here) rather than giving a new, better-justified number, so it was set aside in favor of the broader empty-moments read. Value = 2.5 x Protected(1)=3 = 7.5, Net = 7.5-9 = -1.5. Accepted below Target as part of the Masterwork single-slot-scarcity allowance, same as the rest of this Torso cluster.

Name: Lifeforce Plate (L5)

Name: Dauntless Wrap (L1)
Notes: [Thrice the enhancement's Level] stacks of Protected, granted the first time each day the wearer would be Downed, before that Health loss lands. Name: Fitted Armor
Notes: Reworked from '-1 Might Requirement' (no documented mechanical consequence exists anywhere in rulebook.md for failing a Might Requirement, so the old text was unpriceable) into a flat +1 Physical Resist grant -- the Physical-damage sibling of Elemental-Resistant Armor, except Physical doesn't need a chosen-element pick since it's always relevant. Priced against the assumption that only a tank/bruiser playstyle picks this up (per the designer: the item should be balanced for who actually buys it, not an average character) -- takes 50% more attacks than the party-average baseline, so Physical Resist's own rate scales with the hit-count term: 5.0 x 1.5 = 7.5/point. Value = 1 x 7.5 = 7.5. Landed on Level 2 (Target 6, Net +1.5) over Level 3 (Net -1.5) since this grant carries no risk or guesswork the way Elemental-Resistant Armor's chosen-element bet does -- a tank gets full, guaranteed value every fight, so it doesn't need the same below-Target discount used elsewhere in this cluster for a riskier pick; the built-in self-selection (only the right build wants it) already does the limiting work instead.

Name: Fortified Armor
Grants: Resist:1(conditional, Extra Success trigger, tank assumption 1.5x hits)
Notes: Reworded from 'a red card was flipped' -- a stale reference to an older design where Hearts/Diamonds paired with bonus successes. Current rules tie Extra Successes (and their +1 damage) to matching the attacking Skill's own single governing suit, not a fixed red/black split (rulebook.md), so the accurate current-rules trigger is 'the attack scored an Extra Success' -- this also fixes the item to actually do what it was designed for: soften spikes specifically on the hits that already dealt bonus damage, not an arbitrary half the deck. Priced at the honest suit-match rate (25%, the established suit-scaling convention) x Physical Resist's rate (5.0) x tank assumption (1.5x hits, per the designer -- this is a consistent-protection item for a tank dealing with many attacks): Value = 0.25 x 5.0 x 1.5 = 1.875, Net = 1.875-9 = -7.125, the deepest Net in this cluster. Accepted deliberately, not as a miss: per the designer, this is meant to have a higher ceiling than a flat expected-value model can price, since it's specifically countering burst/spike damage (a real, separately-flagged blind spot in the Resist model -- see balance_weights_notes.md) rather than shaving average damage, and there's real design headroom to expand which enemies can score Extra Successes (e.g. Good Luck to hit) going forward. Preferred leaving this underpowered by the flat model over inflating it to hit a Net the model can't actually justify.

Name: Sash of Deep Pockets
Notes: Bumped to Level 3 and reworked into 'the biggest bag you can wear' -- modeled against Placeholder's Spacious Satchel (I115, Other slot, L3, 60 Gold, 100 cubic meters) at the same price point, scaled down (20 cubic meters, 'about the size of a small closet,' same phrasing style as the Satchel's own text) since the Satchel is meant to stay the enormous option; this item's identity is being worn and always accessible instead. Removal drawback added (everything falls out immediately if taken off) as the countermeasure against using it as a Satchel substitute -- a narrative/logistics deterrent, not priced as a discount since it doesn't affect combat value. Capacity (per-encounter reframe, 2.75) + 2 large-object slots (up from 1, since size is now effectively unrestricted rather than 1m-capped: 2 x 0.917 = 1.833) = 4.583, Target (L3, per-encounter) = 9, Net = -4.42.

Name: Placeholder's Bottomless Belt
Notes: Reframed per the designer's steer: the value isn't an occasional capacity-crunch event, it's the everyday convenience of not juggling what's in easy (1 AP) vs. hard (2 AP) reach -- items that would sit in the backpack now sit in the belt, every fight, not once a day. That's the same AP-saved-on-retrieval logic Quick Draw Belt uses, so this is now scoped per-encounter (Target = Level x3), not once/day (Level x6). Value = 1 realistic retrieval x 1 AP saved (2.75) = 2.75, Net = 2.75-3 = -0.25.

Name: Smuggler's Belt
Grants: FreeRetrieval-equiv:1(capacity), ItemTransfer:1(0 AP, willing ally), Secrecy:2xGoodLuck(0.25 freq)
Notes: Reworked: 8 pouches (up from 5, flavor only -- still under the 3-slot realistic ceiling, no separate capacity credit beyond the shared base). New ability: for 0 AP, transfer an item to a willing ally within sight -- priced as a flat 1-AP-equivalent credit (2.75), not a per-encounter-frequency estimate, per the designer's framing that this is contingent on how many items actually get moved, not assumed combat-frequency use. Secrecy revised: 2x Good Luck (2.4 each = 4.8) at the corrected every-other-day frequency -- since the baseline is per-encounter with 2 encounters/day, 'every other day' = 1 occurrence per 4 encounters = 0.25, not the 0.5 used last round: 4.8 x 0.25 = 1.2. Value = 2.75 (base capacity, per-encounter reframe) + 2.75 (item transfer) + 1.2 (secrecy) = 6.7, Target (L2) = 6, Net = 0.7.

Name: Mendicant's Cord
Notes: MECHANIC REWORKED entirely -- the old flat 2-point Defense-shift ("didn't feel good to the designer") replaced with: on your turn, 0 AP, choose either Dodge&Parry or Vital/Mental/Instinct Defenses; until you choose again, attacks against the chosen group have Bad Luck, the other group Good Luck (reuses Harried's/Vulnerable's own established Defense-group split). Good Luck and Bad Luck are priced identically (2.2 each): Value = 2.2xD, where D = net extra hits landing on the protected group vs. the weakened one. Using the 1.875-hits/player/encounter baseline as the ceiling, D maxes at 1.875 -> best case Value = 4.125, which CANNOT reach Level 2's Target (6) under any circumstance -- a hard structural cap from the encounter's own combat math, not a judgment call. Realistic range: ~1.375 (a genuinely mixed encounter, using Resist's own 2/3-1/3 damage-share split as the read-accuracy proxy) up to near the 4.125 ceiling (a well-read, consistently lopsided encounter). Per the designer, accepted at Level 2 anyway -- many real encounters ARE consistently lopsided, so realized value skews well above the pessimistic blended estimate even though it can never fully close the gap. Reflavored as an actual ring (mendicant-order knotted-cord imagery) while keeping the name; targeting narrowed to self-only (the "or a willing adjacent creature" option was cut). [Supersedes this row's earlier pre-rework value (flat Value=2.0), which priced the original point-shifting mechanic.]

Name: Quick Draw Belt
Notes: Modeled on the Quick Draw Technique (T039, 'It takes you 0 AP to retrieve or store an item, regardless of location') scoped down to one realistic use/encounter rather than always-on, since a Technique is a permanent trait and should stay strictly stronger than replaceable gear covering the same niche. Priced against the backpack case (2 AP normally, saves 2 AP = 5.5), since 'regardless of location' is the whole point of the ability -- this item doesn't carry the Storage family's capacity credit, since its own text doesn't grant extra pouches. Value = 5.5, Net = 5.5-6 = -0.5 (Level 2, per-encounter Target), landing at the Technique's own Level without forcing it. (Superseded the earlier merged 'Belt of the Wayfarer' design, which combined this ability with unlimited-size capacity at Level 3 -- split into this item plus Sash of Deep Pockets' own rework.)

Name: Hair-Trigger Belt
Notes: Same Quick Draw (T039) anchor as Belt of the Wayfarer, but Interrupt-timed instead of a normal action -- lets the wearer react to new information (a revealed threat, an enemy's declared attack) rather than committing blind, which this pricing treats as the value driver for the Level jump over the once/encounter version, not a separate 'reactive premium' on top of the AP math. No unlimited-object-size credit here (kept a distinct identity from Belt of the Wayfarer's capacity focus). Estimated 2 real Interrupt-worthy trigger moments per encounter (an ambush, an emergency swap) -- this specific count is a genuine judgment call with no clean precedent, flagged for revisiting. Each retrieval priced at the backpack-case 2 AP saved (5.5). Value = 2x5.5 = 11.0, Net = 11.0-12 = -1.0 (Level 4). [Wording updated: rules text no longer states an explicit 'twice per encounter' cap -- per the designer, price it as though unlimited, trusting realistic play patterns (about 2 real Interrupt-worthy moments per fight) to hold in practice rather than writing a hard rule. Pricing unchanged (Value 11.0, Net -1.0) since it still reflects the same 2-uses-per-encounter realistic estimate -- a player exceeding that is an earned outcome, not something to price against.]

Name: Belt of the Wayfarer
Notes: Mundane Adventurer's Kit items price at essentially zero (flavor/logistics convenience, same treatment as Jerkin of the Land's nourishment effect -- not a real Value driver). The daily Potion budget is the real component: 'Potions worth up to 2 Levels total' (either two Windrunner's Draughts [L1] or one Thornskin Elixir [L2]) is a point-budget design, not a flat cap -- both spending options land at exactly the same raw value (2x3=6 for two L1 Potions, 1x6=6 for one L2 Potion) since Potion Target scales linearly with Level, so the choice doesn't matter for pricing purposes. Value = 6, Target (L2, once/day -- this component is genuinely a daily resource, unlike the AP-saved-on-retrieval items above) = 12, Net = -6, matching the same -3xLevel shape Dauntless Wrap's intentional discount already established. FLAG for future expansion: only 2 Potions are currently eligible (a deliberate proof-of-concept-sized list per the designer); add more non-healing, non-Poison, non-Grenade buff Potions to the eligible pool as they're created, and consider whether other item types (not just Potions) could eventually round out the daily budget too.

Name: Placeholder's Grasping Gloves
Notes: Scoped-down item version of Tender Telekinesis (T095) -- kept the Technique's own 2 AP cost and fixed the range at 5m (was Skill-Total-scaled) so it doesn't outclass the permanent Technique or require the wearer to have Sorcery/Theurgy. Narrative Utility item (mostly exploration/puzzle value, explicitly barred from attacking) -- priced via the labeled-guess convention, Value = 1/3 x Target = 1/3 x 3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2. Per the designer: deliberately not optimized, a fun quirky Level-1 pickup, not a min-max pick.

Name: Vanishing Gloves
Notes: Once/day, conjures a free Smokejar (I031) into the wearer's hand. Granting a copy of an already-priced Grenade makes this clean to cost directly off that item's own established Value: Value = 6.25 (Smokejar's own Value), Target (once/day, Level x6) = 6, Net = 6.25-6 = 0.25 -- about as tight a fit as this pass has produced. Immaculate Adhesive ('the glue') was considered as the alternative grant but fits less cleanly (would land at Net -1.875).

Name: Armory Gauntlets
Notes: Situational Multiplier tiers per balance_weights.csv: 1=every encounter, 1/2=once/day, 1/3=rarer than daily (niche) -- don't calculate finer gradations, an item landing underpowered here needs redesign, not a more precise discount. Reworked from knightly 'Armory' theming into a smuggling item -- conjures any single weapon at will, 0 AP, and is undetectable by anyone unfamiliar with this specific pair. Two components: (1) conjuring treated as a draw-speed saving, tier-1 (every encounter -- drawing a weapon happens nearly every fight): 1 AP saved x 2.75 = 2.75. (2) Concealment priced like Smuggler's Belt's secrecy, tier-1/3 (rarer than daily -- someone actually searching you): Good Luck-tier (2.4) x 1/3 = 0.8. Value = 2.75+0.8 = 3.55, Target (L1) = 3, Net = 0.55.

Name: Deft Gloves
Notes: Situational Multiplier tiers per balance_weights.csv: 1=every encounter, 1/2=once/day, 1/3=rarer than daily (niche) -- don't calculate finer gradations, an item landing underpowered here needs redesign, not a more precise discount. Broadened from 'Craft for small devices/locks only' to all non-attack Craft flips, per the designer's steer, to see the value this unlocks. Good Luck on a now-unrestricted single Skill: tier-1/2 (once/day -- genuine recurring need, not every fight): 2.4 x 0.5 = 1.2. Tinker's-tools equivalence (no separate equipment needed for small devices) priced as a flat convenience credit, 0.5, same shape as the Storage family's 'removes GM friction' treatment. Value = 1.2+0.5 = 1.7, Target (L2) = 6, Net = -4.3.

Name: Field Surgeon's Handwraps
Notes: Situational Multiplier tiers per balance_weights.csv: 1=every encounter, 1/2=once/day, 1/3=rarer than daily (niche) -- don't calculate finer gradations, an item landing underpowered here needs redesign, not a more precise discount. Good Luck on all Medicine flips -- per the designer, several Techniques call for Medicine flips directly, so this is genuine recurring demand, not a niche trigger: tier-1/2 (once/day). Value = 2.4 x 0.5 = 1.2, Target (L2) = 6, Net = -4.8.

Name: Nimble Fingers
Notes: Situational Multiplier tiers per balance_weights.csv: 1=every encounter, 1/2=once/day, 1/3=rarer than daily (niche) -- don't calculate finer gradations, an item landing underpowered here needs redesign, not a more precise discount. Reworked from an active 'as a Move, opposed Stealth check' ability into a passive Good Luck bonus on Stealth flips made specifically to steal or lift an item unnoticed, per the designer's steer -- matches the Deft Gloves/Field Surgeon's Handwraps pattern. Kept narrow (stealing specifically, not all Stealth), so tier-1/3 applies, not the broader 1/2 Deft Gloves/Field Surgeon's now use: 2.4 x 1/3 = 0.8, Target (L2) = 6, Net = -5.2.

Name: Mighty Mitts
Notes: Situational Multiplier tiers per balance_weights.csv: 1=every encounter, 1/2=once/day, 1/3=rarer than daily (niche) -- don't calculate finer gradations, an item landing underpowered here needs redesign, not a more precise discount. Three components: (1) ignore no-tools penalties on Might-break checks, flat convenience credit 0.5, same shape as Deft Gloves' tinker's-tools clause. (2) Good Luck on Might flips to move/destroy things -- narrow case (excludes Might attacks), tier-1/3: 2.4 x 1/3 = 0.8. Value = 0.5+0.8+1.5 = 2.8, Target (L3) = 9, Net = -6.2.

Name: Gloves of Spatial Distortion

Name: Evertoking Bottle
Notes: Two components. Cover: reuses Smokejar's own established Cover(relocation) rate (1) directly, since this is the same Light Cover-from-smoke mechanic. Debuff zone: a suit-randomized attack (+6 vs Vital Defense) against anyone ending their turn in the cloud -- Necrotic 2 stacks (Spade)/Vulnerable 1 (Club)/Slowed 1 (Diamond)/Crippled 1 (Heart), uniform 25% each. Expected keyword value per landed hit: (6+1+1.1+1.5)/4=2.4, x0.5 on-hit discount (standard convention) = 1.2/instance. Estimated ~2 realized trigger-instances/encounter (same assumption AoE Grenades use) x 0.8 realization (indiscriminate, can catch allies, same AoE downside discount) = 1.2x2x0.8=1.92. Value = 1+1.92 = 2.92, Net = 2.92-3 = -0.08. FLAGGED: the +6 attack bonus is unusually generous for Level 1; used the standard 50% on-hit discount without adjusting upward for it, so this Value may be a real underestimate.

Name: Distant Scroll Cases
Notes: Paired long-distance item/document-sharing cases -- pure logistics/communication, no combat angle. Narrative Utility item: Value = 1/3 x 6 = 2, Net = 2-6 = -4.

Name: Placeholder's Spacious Satchel
Notes: Priced via the Storage capacity model (not Narrative Utility), same reasoning as Sash of Deep Pockets -- this is a direct storage item. Base capacity (2.75, 3-slot ceiling) + 3 large-object slots at the established rate (0.917 each) -- credited the full 3-slot ceiling rather than Sash's 2, since this item's 100-cubic-meter volume and head-sized opening both exceed Sash's own numbers: 2.75 + 3x0.917 = 5.5. Per-encounter Target (L3) = 9, Net = -3.5. Doesn't need Sash's 'falls out if removed' drawback -- not being worn is already a real downside (easier to be separated from) on its own.

Name: Immaculate Spice Rack (cut)
Notes: Cut entirely, not priced -- per the designer, the game has few Craft flips for creating items in actual play, making this item's cooking-specific Good Luck largely irrelevant. Placeholder's Wondrous Workspace (the universal tool-requirement waiver) absorbs its thematic niche instead. Zero cross-references, removed cleanly from items.csv.

Name: Unmovable Bar
Notes: Pure anchor-point prop -- no Skill flip, no combat application. Narrative Utility item: Value = 1/3 x 3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2.

Name: Placeholder's Indelible Instrument

Value = 0 (not even the Narrative Utility token credit), Net = -Target = -3. Not a balance concern, just not what this model prices.

Name: Placeholder's Wondrous Workspace
Notes: Universal tool/kit-requirement waiver for any crafting School -- same shape as Deft Gloves' 'counts as tinker's tools' clause, but much broader (every School, not just small devices), and now the sole tool-substitute item in the catalog since Immaculate Spice Rack's cut. Name: Swim Flippers
Notes: Renamed from Cobblestone Boots; swim with no penalty, at full Speed. No AP/hit-chance anchor -- swimming only costs 1/space from the Athletics budget, the same gentle horizontal rate as jumping, so most reasonably-built characters can likely already swim at full Speed without this. Narrative Utility item: Value = 1/3x3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2. A no-need-to-breathe-underwater clause was considered then cut -- per the designer, that belongs to a different slot's job (see Diver's Necklace, Neck).

Name: Feathered Sandals
Notes: Ignores up to 10m of distance for fall-damage purposes. Moved off plain Narrative Utility once its old "flip to avoid falling damage" wording was found stale (fall damage is a flat calculation now, no flip) -- this prevents guaranteed Health loss, priced via Health's own guaranteed-harm rate (4/point) directly. Constructed representative case (6m fall, baseline reduction 3, matching the "baseline stat=3" pattern used for Body/Agility elsewhere): Prevented = (6-3)x4 = 12 raw, realized at the 1/3 "rarer than daily, niche" tier: 12x1/3 = 4.0. Net = 4.0-3 = +1.0 (Level 1). The 6m/reduction-3 case is a constructed placeholder, not a firm derivation -- flagged as a first stab, open to a better representative fall if one turns up.

Name: Lightfoot Shoes (L1)
Notes: Flat +Level Speed, worn continuously -- uses the newly-derived Speed(permanent/gear) rate (2.54375/point, not the single-instance 0.55/point) since this is live for the whole encounter, not a one-shot move: derived from the game's own AP economy (4 AP/turn, 2 AP/attack, half of turns spend all 4 AP on 2 attacks, the other half split 85/15 between a second move and a wasted/utility AP) -> 4.625 moves/encounter x 0.55 = 2.54375. Value = 1x2.54375 = 2.54. Lands at a flat ~85% of Target every Level -- accepted as a modest, real shortfall (not a pricing-model blind spot the way Torso Resist's allowance was, since Speed's 0.55 base rate already is the felt-value number).

Name: Slipstream Sandals
Notes: Once/encounter, 0 AP, Teleport 3 meters -- priced as an attack-enabler, not raw movement (per the designer, "you only use them if you need the extra to hit a breakpoint"; does nothing on a turn already in range, does nothing if too far out for even the extra 3m to matter). Value = cost of landing the attack it enables (2 AP x 2.75 = 5.5) x frequency it's the deciding factor (100%, per the designer, since a player who takes this finds a way to use it well basically every fight) = 5.5. Net = 5.5-6 = -0.5. 3m deliberately anchored to "one stack short of Slowed's own 4-stack hard cap" (guarantees the crucial move still gets through under near-maximal Slowed without fully trivializing it), not an arbitrary flavor number.

Name: Vaulting Boots
Notes: Once/encounter, 1 AP, jump up to 10m in any direction -- rebuilt after the running-start rule was cut outright (the old "without requiring a running start or a flip" wording implied a flip-guarantee credit that no longer applies; replaced with a Good Luck grant instead). Value = attack-enabler (same basis as Slipstream Sandals, 5.5) + fall-safety flat credit (1) + vertical-jump-flexibility bypassing the Athletics budget's steep 2-per-space vertical cost (+2, one step above fall-safety's own +1) + Good Luck on jump-related flips at the 1/3 "rarer than daily" tier (2.4x1/3 = 0.8) = 9.3. Net = 9.3-9 = +0.3 -- lands close to Target on its own, no accept-below-Target allowance needed.

Name: Greaves of the Stalwart Guardian
Notes: Redesigned from a guessed 3-component Level 5 item (immovability, ignore 3 degrees Difficult Terrain, 5 charges/encounter to negate Slowed) down to 2 components at Level 2, after features.csv showed Push (Lodestone, F010) and Slowed (Hamstring F008/Frigid F071) are both cheapest-tier Basic Features on the most generic, broadly-available Buildable techniques -- not niche at all. Difficult Terrain component dropped entirely (duplicates Surestride Boots' own job at no extra value; the rule itself floors movement at 1m/action past degree 2, so ignoring 3 degrees protects no more than Surestride's 2 already does). Slowed-negation replaced with outright immunity (dropping an unpriceable 5-charge tracked resource). Per the designer, the two triggers split one shared "about half of fights feature either a Push- or a Slow-relevant threat" -- 25% each: immovability representative hit (8m x 0.55/meter = 4.4) x 0.25 = 1.1; Slowed immunity full cap (17.6) x 0.25 = 4.4. Value = 1.1+4.4 = 5.5. Rather than stretch the effect to justify Level 5, dropped to Level 2 (Target 6). Net = 5.5-6 = -0.5, the same modest-shortfall shape as Surestride Boots' own -0.75.

Name: Shadowcat Slippers
Notes: Unconditional wall-running at full Speed for the whole encounter -- structurally the same "permanent, flat-credit, vertical-Athletics-budget-bypass" shape as Vaulting Boots' own +2 rider, but continuously available rather than gated to one guaranteed use. Not built on a hard per-meter/per-move rate -- Vaulting Boots' own +2 was already a soft, constructed flat credit, and multiplying a soft guess by an assumed frequency compounds uncertainty rather than resolving it. Assumed ~2 meaningful uses/encounter where vertical mobility actually matters (same order of magnitude as Greaves of the Warlock King's own "2 uses" figure): Value ~ 2x2 = 4. Net = 4-6 = -2 -- better than the original Narrative Utility -4, but flagged explicitly as the least-grounded number of the Feet-slot items revisited this pass, likely still wants a real redesign pass rather than being treated as settled.

Name: Greaves of the Warlock King
Notes: Once/turn, 1 AP, Teleport 2xSpeed meters (8m at baseline Speed 4) -- a two-mode engine, not a single flat rate, since it's repeatable up to 5 times across a Baseline encounter: cheap-saver mode (gap already <=9m, just does the same job for less AP -- 1 AP saved x 2.75 = 2.75/use) and rescue mode (gap 10-13m, the full "costs the attack" zone from the range breakpoints derivation -- full attack-enabler value, 5.5/use). Per the designer, a player who takes this finds ways to make the extra margin count, landing at 2 rescue + 2 cheap-saver uses/encounter: Value = 2x5.5 + 2x2.75 = 11+5.5 = 16.5. Net = 16.5-15 = +1.5.

Name: Surestride Boots
Notes: Simplified from "ignores 2 degrees of Difficult Terrain" to "ignores the effects of Difficult Terrain" -- a pure wording simplification, not a power change, since Difficult Terrain's own rate hard-caps at degree 2 (0/2.75/8.25/8.25 for degrees 0/1/2/3+; the rule itself floors movement throughput at 1m/action once terrain hits degree 2, so degree 3+ was never worse to a mover than degree 2 already was). Value stays at the full capped rate, 8.25 -- the cleanest, most directly-derived number in the whole Feet slot, no construction or guesswork needed. Net = 8.25-9 = -0.75, unchanged through both wording passes.

Name: Confident Cap
Notes: Redesigned from a defunct "front/Concession" social-contest mechanic (referencing rules -- "front," "Concession" -- that no longer exist under the current Statements/Pressure system) into a Good Luck grant on Persuasion flips made outside a social contest. Value = 2.4 (Good Luck) x 0.5 (1/2 "genuine recurring demand" tier) = 1.2. Pegged to Level 2 (not the model's own preferred Level 1, which would read Net -1.8) to match existing same-shape Hands-slot precedent (Field Surgeon's Handwraps, Deft Gloves, Nimble Fingers, all Level 2, none yet run through this model) rather than trusting the model over live precedent. Net = 1.2-6 = -4.8. Part of a four-item Good-Luck-on-a-Skill consolidation with Cap of Smug Confidence/Sympathetic Hat/Hat of Disguise; Stoic Skullcap (I169) retired from this family entirely (see its own CUT row).

Name: Cap of Smug Confidence
Notes: Same consolidated Good-Luck-on-a-Skill family and pricing as Confident Cap (I060) -- see that row for the full derivation. Value = 2.4x0.5 = 1.2, Net = 1.2-6 = -4.8.

Name: Sympathetic Hat
Notes: Same consolidated Good-Luck-on-a-Skill family and pricing as Confident Cap (I060) -- see that row for the full derivation. Value = 2.4x0.5 = 1.2, Net = 1.2-6 = -4.8.

Name: Stoic Skullcap (cut)
Notes: Retired from the Head social-hat consolidation -- its flavor (resisting OTHERS' persuasion) is defensive, not offensive, and doesn't map cleanly onto the family's "Good Luck on your own Skill" shape the way Confident Cap/Cap of Smug Confidence/Sympathetic Hat do. Per the designer, its name and flavor ("a sense of calm and clarity... that intensifies the more another tries to menace or win them over") are deliberately reserved for a future Neck-slot item dealing with Pressure directly, matching Neck's "niche, boring, passive utility" lane better than an offensive Skill-buff family did anyway (see IDEAS_BACKLOG.md). Removed from items.csv.

Name: Hat of Disguise
Notes: New item, a fourth Skill hat in the same family as Confident Cap/Cap of Smug Confidence/Sympathetic Hat -- Masquerade targets Insight Defense and isn't one of the three Skills a Statement uses (Presence/Rapport/Persuasion), confirmed as a genuinely separate mechanic before drafting, not a fourth flavor of the same thing. Same pricing shape: Value = 2.4 (Good Luck) x 0.5 (1/2 tier) = 1.2. Pegged to Level 2 to match the other three. Net = 1.2-6 = -4.8. "No Disguise Kit needed" clause left unpriced -- kits are cheap and common, a flavor-consistent convenience rather than a real value swing.

Name: Cowl of Tranquility
Notes: Cut from a Level 1-5 charge-based range (charges scaled 1xLevel but Target scaled 3xLevel -- an ABSOLUTE, worsening-with-Level shortfall no Level fix alone could solve) down to a fixed Level 2 with outright immunity. features.csv confirms Taunted is just as common as Push/Slowed (Distracting, F004, Basic on a universal technique); no comparable Frightened-inflicting feature was found. Solved for the charge count Level 2's Target (6) would need: charges x 2.2 (Taunted/Frightened's rate) x 0.5 (1/2 tier) = Target -> charges ~ 5.45; 5 charges lands at Value = 5x2.2x0.5 = 5.5, Net = -0.5 -- but per the designer, 5 charges already covers realistic Taunted/Frightened exposure in a fight so completely that tracking it as a resource is pointless theater, functionally equivalent to outright immunity. Simplified to match (wording-only, same move as Greaves of the Stalwart Guardian's Slowed immunity and Surestride Boots' "ignore all") -- Value/Net unchanged.

Name: Mask of Night
Notes: Negates the wearer's own darkness-related sight penalty (own sight-flips only -- not the attacker's-difficulty-seeing-the-wearer side, a different beneficiary this item doesn't touch). Real anchor: total darkness counts as Heavy Cover, which gives Bad Luck twice on sight-related flips. Value = 2 x 2.2 (Bad Luck, mirrors Good Luck's rate) x 0.5 (1/2 "genuine recurring demand" tier, same as the social hats and Cowl of Tranquility) = 2.2. Net = 2.2-3 = -0.8.

Name: Headband of Telepathy
Notes: Telepathic communication with one seen creature within 20m, for the rest of the scene. Per the designer, confirmed as-is deliberately -- no numeric anchor exists or is being sought, a "gut feeling, niche, and that's fine" item, not one meant to ever get a harder anchor. Narrative Utility formula: Value = 1/3x3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2.

Name: Lens of Daybreak
Notes: Good Luck on sight-specific Awareness flips. Per the designer, sight-based Awareness checks are genuinely common (spotting stealthing enemies, general perception), but the payoff per success is soft/narrative rather than a guaranteed hard one, confirming the 1/2 "genuine recurring demand" tier rather than the full "every encounter" one -- same reasoning as Mask of Night, just for a different sight-related trigger. Value = 2.4x0.5 = 1.2. Net = 1.2-6 = -4.8 -- the biggest shortfall among the Head slot's ½-tier items, since Awareness-specifically-sight is a narrower Skill-use than Mask of Night's broader darkness-negation.

Name: Wizardly Hat of Tam the Tipsy
Notes: Regain the use of a burned Encounter Technique (Level <= the Alcohol's own Level) whenever the wearer drinks Alcohol -- redesigned so drinking from the hat's own internal 12-dose stock costs 0 AP (first-pass 2-AP-to-drink version read as a net LOSS below Level 4, since the AP opportunity cost of 2x2.75=5.5 ate more than the benefit). Gold's established rate (1.5, Locked) applied for the first time in this document: Alcohol is worth 1.5xLevel raw Value. A technique-refresh's own worth has no established anchor, so -- per the designer's working, unverified assumption -- it's treated as equal to a same-Level item (Levelx3), making net benefit per matched-Level use exactly Alcohol's own Value again (1.5xLevel). At Level 3, 2 uses/encounter exactly hits Target: 2x4.5 = 9, Net = 0. Flagged, not resolved: with 0 AP cost and a 12-dose reserve, the real ceiling isn't anything this item controls anymore -- a character cycling through 3-4 Techniques in a hard fight could plausibly trigger this 3+ times (Value 13.5+, Net +4.5 or more). Left as-is per the designer -- a legacy item pending a future Alcohol-cost Technique suite (see IDEAS_BACKLOG.md), not something being actively rebalanced today.

Name: Crown of Glory
Notes: SET ASIDE, NOT RESOLVED -- flagged explicitly rather than accepted below Target like the rest of this slot. Once/day, 0 AP, wearer + up to 4 allies who can see them each draw a card. Value = 5x2.7 (Card) = 13.5 against the once/day Target=Levelx6=30, Net=-16.5 -- the largest raw gap anywhere in the Head slot. A "wearer + 2xLevel allies" scaling formula was worked out as a possible numeric fix (Net +2.1 at L1 down to -0.3 at L5, a tight fit), but per the designer the deeper concern isn't the Level-scaling at all -- it's whether a Head-slot item should be generating extra cards for the whole party in the first place. Generic party-wide card generation reads as more of a capstone-tier effect than a normal equipment-slot one. Set aside rather than fixed; revisit once the rest of the equipment slots have had a first pass, to work out what a genuinely capstone-appropriate Head effect looks like, rather than patch the current mechanic's numbers.

Name: Cloak of Caches
Notes: Produces mundane adventuring gear (rope, flint and steel, a bowl, twine, and similar) on demand, one of each at a time. No combat mechanic. Value = 1/3x3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2.

Name: Diver's Necklace
Notes: Breathe water perfectly. No combat mechanic. Value = 1/3x3 = 1, Net = 1-3 = -2. Confirms an earlier call directly: Swim Flippers' (Feet) water-breathing clause was added then cut per the designer ("that would be a different slot's job") -- this is that slot, already live with exactly that effect at exactly this Narrative Utility price.

Name: Choker of Silent Whispers (cut)
Notes: Removed -- checked against Headband of Telepathy (Head, also Level 1) and found to be a strictly WORSE version of the same idea, not a genuine alternative: half the range (10m vs 20m), a single message instead of a standing "rest of the scene" channel, and a visible tell ("will be able to tell... if they see the wearer whispering") Headband of Telepathy doesn't have. Per the designer, remote-communication effects belong on Head, not Neck -- Headband of Telepathy is the correct version of the idea, this was a redundant, strictly-inferior reskin on the wrong slot.

Name: Shroud of Shadowy Stillness
Notes: Good Luck on Stealth flips while wearing the shroud and remaining still -- same Good-Luck-on-a-Skill shape as the Head hats: Value = 2.4x0.5 = 1.2, unchanged. Per the designer, dropped from Level 2 to Level 1 rather than matching the Head hats' Level-2 peg -- unlike those, no existing same-shape item elsewhere in the catalog pulls this one toward Level 2, so it stays on the model's own preferred fit. Net = 1.2-3 = -1.8.

Name: Watcher's Mantle
Notes: Never sleep, rest on your own schedule instead. No combat mechanic -- pure Narrative Utility. Value = 1/3x6 = 2, Net = 2-6 = -4. Name: Shawl of the Land
Notes: Two components. +1 Health from a full night's rest: Health's own guaranteed-harm rate applied directly, 1x4 = 4. "Doesn't need to eat or drink": a real anchor instead of the usual Narrative Utility fallback -- Travel Rations' own Level-1 baseline material (Total Materials:1, no type) is worth its Level in Gold per convert.py's crafting convention (1 Gold), converted through the established Gold=1.5 (Locked) rate to 1.5 raw Value. Value = 4+1.5 = 5.5. Target = 6 (Level 2). Net = -0.5 -- a clean, close fit. KNOWN INCONSISTENCY, kept deliberately: both components are daily-cadence (once/rest), not per-encounter -- under the once/day Target=Levelx6 convention used elsewhere (Crown of Glory, Choker of Defiance) this should really check against Target=12, which would read as badly undervalued rather than a clean -0.5. Name: Cape of Many Pockets (cut)
Notes: Removed -- a clean duplicate of Belt's own established lane ("carrying items"), not just a thematic overlap. Two existing Belt items already do this exact job, better: Placeholder's Bottomless Belt (I189, Level 1, 20 pouches for small objects -- the same "many pouches" shape, more pouches, a third the Level) and Sash of Deep Pockets (I105, Level 3, 20 cubic meters of capacity-gated storage -- bigger and more flexible at the same Level). Name: Snowfall Drape
Notes: Reworked from scratch -- the old "3-space line, [Level] degrees" scaling both over- and under-delivered simultaneously: Difficult Terrain's own rate hard-caps at degree 2 (0/2.75/8.25/8.25 for degrees 0/1/2/3+), so Level 3-5 bought nothing extra, while the line footprint blew past Target even at Level 2 under a "clever player bogging down enemies" framing (2-4 creatures caught). New: footprint changed from a 3-space line to Burst 1 (worst-case straight-through crossing drops from 3m to 2m); degrees fixed at 2 (no longer Level-scaled -- a fixed magnitude, Level now just sets where it sits against Target); crossing cost stepped, not linear (0 or 1 extra action -- 1 AP's value, 2.75 -- per space actually crossed, nothing between). Priced at 3 creatures caught, each crossing the full 2m diameter: Value = 3x2.75 = 8.25. Fixed at Level 3 (Target 9). Net = 8.25-9 = -0.75 -- a clean fit.

Name: Choker of Defiance (L1)
Notes: Reworked in three ways: timing moved to an Interrupt after a flip (adds sifted cards' suits to that flip's own suit pool, matching the window Play from hand already uses); suit-pool credit properly derived rather than folded into Sift's own 0.60/card rate (each sifted card is an independent 1/4 chance to match the flip's suit, worth 1/4 x 2 [Extra Success] x 0.5 [not every flip cares] = 0.25/card at the naive floor, bumped to 0.30/card as a designer judgment call for suits sometimes triggering more than a plain Extra Success -- combined 0.60+0.30 = 0.90/card); a locking clause kept deliberately (spending a charge locks the choker until the wearer's next full night's rest, "use it or lose it," stopping a clever player from freely stacking the deck for the next adventuring day). 2xLevel charges, each spending 1 to Sift 3 cards: Value = 2xLevelx3x0.90 = 5.4xLevel = 5.4. Name: Cloak of One Thousand Feathers
Notes: Whenever the wearer would fall, they glide instead (5m down + 5m horizontal, wearer's choice), ignoring all fall effects regardless of distance -- no cap, unlike Feathered Sandals' 10m ceiling. Name: Cloak of Faces (cut)

Name: Worry Token (L2)
Grants: SuitKeyedSift:charges(Hearts=heal1, Clubs=Hasted x3, Diamonds=+2atk-Shadow, Spades=filter2, once/day convention)
Notes: Reworked from scratch from a GM-secret random table (3 charges/day, mostly-nothing plus six vague/broken effects, GM-fiat branch selection -- doesn't fit a game this card-driven) into a suit-keyed Sift mechanic: spend 1 charge to Sift 1 card, the suit determines the effect, each built from that suit's own established RULES_DESIGN.md archetype identity rather than an arbitrary pick -- Hearts: heal 1 Shallow Health (4.0, Hearts' healing-scales-with-Hearts hook). Name: Ring of Charming, Assertive, or Bold Statements (cut)
Notes: Removed -- Good Luck on a specific social Skill's Statement (Rapport if Charming, Persuasion if Assertive, Presence if Bold; chosen at creation), the exact same shape as Confident Cap/Cap of Smug Confidence/Sympathetic Hat (Head) with no real differentiation beyond the slot it's worn on.
